question: A line has gradient $-\tfrac{2}{9}$.
Find the gradient of a line perpendicular to it.

wrong.why: flipped the fraction, kept the sign

trap: Flip the fraction AND change the sign.

beats.say: Most students get this wrong. A line has gradient negative two over nine. What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to it?
Pause. What do you think the next step is?
Many write negative nine over two. They flip the fraction, but keep the negative sign.
Flipping is right. But perpendicular gradients multiply to negative one, so the sign must change too.
So M two is negative one, divided by negative two over nine. That is nine over two.
Check. Negative two over nine, times nine over two, is negative one.
Remember: flip the fraction, and change the sign.

verify:
m1 = Rational(-2, 9); m2 = Rational(9, 2); wrong = Rational(-9, 2)
assert m1 * m2 == -1
assert -1 / m1 == m2
assert m1 * wrong != -1

youtube.title: Perpendicular gradient: the sign trap
youtube.description: A line has gradient −2/9. What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to it? Most students flip the fraction and stop. Flip it AND change the sign: m₁ × m₂ = −1.
